subject: Re: Customer security questionnaire — data residency & retention boundaries
messages:

Subject: Acme questionnaire: geo & retention scoping (attached)

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for taking this. Attached is our standard security questionnaire focused on data residency and retention. A couple of quick asks up front:

- Can Redwood confirm which regions hosted API request data may be stored or traversed?
- What are the default retention windows for request logs, inference inputs (prompt text) and model outputs? Are there options to shorten them?
- What is the practical deletion timeline if we request tenant-only data erasure (including backups)?

We'd prefer short, explicit answers we can drop into our procurement review.

Ian
Security Ops — Acme Payments

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Ian —

Appreciate the document. High-level answers below so you can share with procurement; attaching a concise playbook for the erasure timeline. If you want we can convert these into explicit SLA language for the contract.

1) Regions/traversal:
- Default: Hosted API endpoints are served from the region selected by the customer at account creation. By default for Acme (US account) data is processed and stored in our US regions (us-west-2 and us-east-1 redundancy).
- Transit: Requests may transit other Redwood control-plane endpoints for routing/observability but payloads are not persisted outside customer region unless explicitly configured.
- Regional pinning: For Hosted API customers we support region pinning; we can add region locking in the contract.

2) Retention windows (defaults / configurable):
- Request logs (routing/ingest metadata): 90 days default; configurable down to 7 days on dedicated support plans.
- Inference inputs (full prompt text): Ephemeral by default — retained for 30 days for quality & abuse monitoring, can be limited to 0 days (not retained) with flag in account settings plus a contractual commitment on our hosted plan.
- Model outputs: Treated the same as inputs; default 30 days, configurable to 0.

3) Deletion timeline (tenant erasure) — practical steps: 
- Standard hosted deletion request (self-serve API): we begin purge within 24 hours and complete primary-store deletion within 72 hours.
- Backups & snapshots: removed on next backup rotation; for hosted customers the practical completion window is typically 14 days.
- Global restore points / cold archives: if any and only if a customer opts into long-term logs for troubleshooting, the maximum completion is 90 days.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-deletion-playbook-v1.3.pdf (playbook with step-by-step timelines & audit hooks).

Next steps: I can provide a short paragraph for your procurement team that we can include in the MSA describing region commitments and the deletion timelines above.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-hosted-deletion-playbook-v1.3.pdf)

Karthik — quick clarifying note for Ian if you want to include it:

- When we say 'ephemeral' / '0 days' retention for inputs/outputs, we mean: we can disable persistent storage of full-text prompts and outputs in our long-term stores and logs. However, short-lived artifacts (KV cache for in-flight generation acceleration) are held in-memory and flushed per-request; they are not searchable post-request.
- Anonymization option: For customers concerned about PII, we offer a pre-ingest redaction hook (managed or self-hosted) that strips identifiers before they hit servers — useful when you want functional logs but no raw PII.

I'll also flag the 14-day backup rotation to legal as "practical completion" and offer a contract clause that requires Redwood to provide an attestation once the purge reaches completion.

—Lauren
Director, Customer Success Operations

Ian

Ian —

Thanks for the clarifying questions; see direct wording below you can paste into the SOW/MSA.

Proposed MSA language (suggested clauses):

1) Regional processing and storage: "Redwood Inference will process and store Customer data in the geographic region(s) selected by the Customer. For Accounts designated as US-region, Redwood will maintain primary and redundant copies within US regions (currently us-west-2 and us-east-1). Redwood will not persist Customer data to regions outside the selected geographic scope, except as necessary for ephemeral control-plane routing and as explicitly agreed in writing.

2) Data retention and configurable limits: "By default, Redwood retains request logs for 90 days and inference inputs/outputs for 30 days for quality monitoring and abuse detection. Upon Customer request and subject to account configuration or an executed addendum, Redwood will implement reduced retention settings including 0-day retention (no persistent storage of inference inputs/outputs)."

3) Tenant erasure and backup handling: "Upon receipt of a verified tenant erasure request, Redwood will mark data for immediate logical deletion and begin primary-store purging within 72 hours. Backups and long-term snapshots will be removed on their next scheduled rotation; Redwood estimates practical completion of all recoverable copies within 14 days for standard hosted accounts. If Customer requires accelerated timeline or certified proof of destruction, Customer and Redwood will agree on a remediation plan in writing (may incur one-time fees)."

Operational notes: 
- Logical delete + delete-marker approach means data is made non-restorable from the active dataset immediately; restore from backups is possible until snapshots expire/rotate.
- The 0-day retention option for Hosted API is available via a signed addendum for customers requiring contractual guarantees; self-serve toggles exist for Dedicated and Private deployments.

I'll paste the suggested clauses into a one-page insert and send as a PDF. If you want an attestation template (SOC-style) we can provide our erasure confirmation form after purge completion.

Best,
Karthik
